without meeting,

Suddenly, on Wednesday, the eighth of the first month of the Arabs [Muharram],
in the year six hundred and fifty-six [of the Hijra],
which is the year 1569
1569 of the Greeks,
Baiju Noyan and his forces first approached a place called the Tomb of Ahmad on the western side of Baghdad,
and the people of Baghdad also advanced.
And they met one another,
and the side of Baiju Noyan was broken,
and the people of Baghdad triumphed with victory.
Now Amir Sulayman Shah with his force was upon the wall of Baghdad.
And when it became evening,
Ibn Kurr the elder said to the young Devatdar:
"Now that God has given us victory,
it is right that we enter our houses and rest,
and then go out again and engage [the enemy]."
He, however, acted haughtily and was not willing to enter,
and they all spent the night outside.
And because the people of Baghdad were encamped in a low-lying place,
the Tatars went and broke open against them a breach in the great dyke of the waters of the Tigris,
and the waters flooded over them in the middle of the night.
And they began fleeing from the midst of the waters,
and their bows, their arrows, and their sword scabbards became soaked.
And when morning dawned,
the Tatars, the men of Hulagu's wing, turned upon them.
And the battle dragged on until nine hours of Thursday,
and the side of the people of Baghdad was defeated and routed,
and Ibn Kurr was killed,
and the Devatdar fled and entered the city.
Then Baiju and his forces came and encamped on the western side of Baghdad,
and Hulagu encamped on the eastern side,
on Monday, the thirteenth of the first month,
and he mounted a fierce assault against the city,
facing the crown of the Caliph's palace.
And when hope was cut off, that miserable Caliph al-Musta'sim
called Ibn al-Alqami his vizier,
and Najm al-Din Abd al-Ghani ibn Darnus, and Mar Makkikha the Catholicos,
and ordered them to take an abundance of gold,
and royal gifts,
and Arab horses,
and to bring out the envoys of the Tatars from prison,
and clothe them,
and give them lavish gifts,
and go with them to the King of Kings,
and sue for terms for the life of the Caliph.
